basic_identification.full_title: Steel Plate for Pressure Vessel for Intermediate and High Temperature Service Including Boilers — Specification (Fourth Revision)
basic_identification.sector_category: Metallurgical Engineering (approved by the Metallurgical Engineering Division Council and finalized by the Wrought Steel Products Sectional Committee of the Bureau of Indian Standards)

scope.summary: This standard specifies the requirements, testing methods, and quality standards for steel plates used in the fabrication of boilers and pressure vessels operating under intermediate and high temperature service. It details three main grades of steel (Grades 1, 2, and 3) based on chemical composition and mechanical properties.

certification_and_marking.certification_status: Strict Statutory Mandatory Certification. Under the 'Steel and Steel Products (Quality Control) Order, 2024' issued by the Ministry of Steel, Government of India, all steel plates for pressure vessels and boilers conforming to IS 2002 must carry the BIS Standard Mark (ISI Mark) to be legally manufactured, stocked, sold, or imported. Precious metal hallmarking is completely inapplicable to heavy structural steel plate products, as it is reserved strictly for gold and silver jewelry under national BIS frameworks [Image 21].

requirements.detail: Every conforming steel plate must bear the BIS Standard Mark (ISI Mark) under a valid licence issued by the Bureau of Indian Standards [Image 21].

Each plate must be legibly and indelibly marked with: a) Manufacturer's name or recognized trade-mark; b) Cast/heat number or identification mark by which the steel can be traced to its ladle analysis, along with the individual plate number to allow correlation with the test certificate; and c) The direction of final rolling [Image 21].

If any test piece fails to meet specified results, two additional random tests must be carried out on the same lot. Both re-tests must conform to standard limits, otherwise the entire lot is rejected [Image 21].
If requested by the purchaser at the time of inquiry, each accepted plate must be painted with one coat of boiled linseed oil or an approved rust preventive material [Image 21].

Grade 1 plates must meet a tensile strength of 360 to 480 MPa. The minimum yield stress varies by thickness: 235 MPa (<= 16 mm), 225 MPa (> 16 to 40 mm), 215 MPa (> 40 to 60 mm), 200 MPa (> 60 to 100 mm), and 185 MPa (> 100 to 350 mm). Minimum elongation on a 5.65√So gauge length must be 24% for thickness <= 60 mm and 23% for thickness > 60 mm [2].

Grade 2 plates must meet a tensile strength of 410 to 530 MPa. The minimum yield stress varies by thickness: 265 MPa (<= 16 mm), 255 MPa (> 16 to 40 mm), 245 MPa (> 40 to 60 mm), 215 MPa (> 60 to 100 mm), and 200 MPa (> 100 to 350 mm). Minimum elongation must be 22% for thickness <= 60 mm and 21% for thickness > 60 mm [2].

Laminar-type discontinuities <= 25 mm in length that are visible to the unaided eye on plate edges as prepared for shipment are acceptable and do not require further exploration. All larger discontinuities must be explored [3].

Discontinuities are considered continuous when located in the same plate within 5 percent of the plate thickness and separated by a distance less than the length of the smaller of two adjacent discontinuities [3].

plain_language_summary.summary: IS 2002 : 2024 is the strict national Indian Standard specification governing carbon steel plates used to fabricate boilers, pressure vessels, and heat exchangers operating under intermediate and high temperatures. In accordance with India's national Steel Quality Control Order, all boiler-quality plates manufactured, imported, or sold in the country must carry the mandatory BIS Standard Mark (ISI Mark). This fourth revision establishes tight mechanical limits—including tensile strengths of up to 530 MPa and minimum yield stresses matched to plate thickness—as well as strict quality controls, such as edge laminar discontinuity limits (maximum 25 mm without exploration) and mandatory heat-traceability markings stamped directly on each plate.
